title: kubeadm join backoff lab notes
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for recurring issue where freshly provisioned nodes attempt 'kubeadm join' but kubelet goes into crashloop/backoff and node remains NotReady. Goal is to capture commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps for repro/mitigation.

Context and symptoms:
- Provisioning flow: cloud-init -> apt install containerd / kubeadm / kubelet -> write /etc/containerd/config.toml -> systemctl enable --now containerd && kubelet -> kubeadm join --token ... --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash ...
- Observed behavior: 'kubeadm join' prints success, kubelet registers node, then shortly after node transitions to NotReady and kubelet crashes/backoffs. Sometimes kubelet logs contain TLS bootstrap errors or cgroup resource rejections.
- Frequency: intermittent on GKE-like custom images and on baremetal lab nodes. More frequent after recent containerd upgrade to 1.7.x and kernel 6.x on lab infra.

Commands run (timestamped-ish):
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
  -> snippet: "E1103 12:21:54.123456   887 kubelet_node_status.go:121] Failed to get node info: node 'ip-10-0-8-45' not found"
  -> then: "E1103 12:21:54.223789   887 server.go:123] TLS bootstrap failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"

- sudo systemctl status kubelet -l
  -> snippet: "Active: failed (Result: exit-code) since ...; Main PID: 887 (code=exited, status=1/FAILURE)"

- kubeadm join --v=5 ...
  -> shows join complete, wrote kubelet.conf, created bootstrap-kubelet.conf, but later kubelet kept failing to rotate client certs.

- ls -l /etc/kubernetes/pki && ls -l /var/lib/kubelet/pki
  -> bootstrap files present, but /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet-client-current.pem missing on failures.

- crictl ps -a && sudo ctr -n k8s.io images ls
  -> containerd running, images present. No obvious OOM.

- sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init.log | grep kubelet -n
  -> discovered ordering race where kubelet systemd unit started before containerd socket available (containerd starting took ~3s longer due to overlayfs mount).

- sudo journalctl -u containerd -b | tail -n 80
  -> occasional "failed to serve grpc: listen unix /run/containerd/containerd.sock: bind: address already in use" when cloud-init recreated socket file quickly across reboots.

Quick local reproduction (lab):
- repro steps tried:
  1) boot node image with systemd unit modifications (kubelet.service had 'After=containerd.service' but no 'Requires='; switched to 'After=containerd.service containerd.socket' + 'Requires=containerd.service').
  2) forced slow containerd startup by adding ExecStartPre=/bin/sleep 4 to containerd.service -> reduced failures in small sample.
  3) tried enabling kubelet to wait for network-online.target -> no impact.

Error snippets collected: (raw-ish)
- "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" on kubelet TLS bootstrap attempt.
- "failed to rotate certificate: write /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet-client-current.pem: no space left on device" (on one node where ephemeral partition was small).
- "cgroups: cannot write ...: no such file or directory" when kubelet attempted to set cpuset for a pod -> kernel/cgroup mismatch (systemd driver vs cgroup v2 confusion).
- "kubelet: failed to create plugin watch: error opening /run/containerd/containerd.sock: permission denied" after docker->containerd migration; turned out to be incorrect socket group/permissions.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Startup ordering race: kubelet starts before containerd/socket -> kubelet fails to start cleanly and cert rotation fails intermittently. Evidence: adding Requires/After reduces frequency.
2) File system / partition sizing: if /var is low, cert writes fail -> kubelet fails. Evidence: one node showed ENOSPC.
3) Cgroup/config mismatch: kernel + container runtime config results in kubelet errors related to cpuset and cgroup v1/v2 expectations. Evidence: kernel 6.x on repro nodes and containerd config set to systemd cgroup driver in some images.
4) TLS CA mismatch in bootstrap path: sometimes discovery token CA cert hash mismatch when cluster CA rotates. Evidence: sporadic x509 errors even after join succeeded.
5) race with cloud-init or config management re-applying files (restarting containerd or rewriting /run socket) -> permission errors or socket binding issues.

Fixes tried and results:
- Added 'Requires=containerd.service' to kubelet unit and 'After=containerd.socket' -> reduced failures from ~25% to ~3% in lab runs (n=40).
- Added preflight check in provisioning script to ensure /var has >150MB free -> eliminated ENOSPC repro.
- Updated containerd socket permissions during provisioning: chown root:docker /run/containerd/containerd.sock; chmod 660 -> fixed permission denied in 2/2 repros.
- For cgroup issues, tried forcing containerd cgroup driver to 'systemd' and booting kernel with 'systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=0' -> mixed results; needs deeper testing across kernel versions.
- For x509 bootstrap flakiness, added retry loop around kubelet certificate rotation (hacky) but need proper fix: ensure kube-apiserver CA data is stable and discovery token generation isn't racing with CA rotation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is there a single root cause that explains both TLS x509 errors and socket permission failures? Likely not — multiple independent root causes.
- Add explicit readiness ordering in systemd units for kubelet to depend on network-online + containerd socket + cloud-init-complete.target. Prototype systemd drop-in at /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-deps.conf.
- Add kubeadm join wrapper that verifies container runtime socket is present and owned by correct group prior to 'kubeadm join'.
- Re-run full matrix tests across kernel 5.15, 6.1, 6.4 with containerd 1.6 vs 1.7 and different cgroup setups. Create test matrix in infra repo.
- Investigate possibility that our cloud-init script is restarting containerd after kubeadm join in some flows (due to unit file re-write). If so, kubelet certificate rotation might be interrupted.

Notes to self / short commands to repro/fix on a live node: 
- Ensure socket present: until [ -S /run/containerd/containerd.sock ]; do echo waiting; sleep 1; done
- Verify ownership: sudo stat -c '%U:%G %a' /run/containerd/containerd.sock
- Force kubelet to re-bootstrap logs: sudo systemctl stop kubelet; sudo rm -rf /var/lib/kubelet/pki/*; sudo systemctl start kubelet; sudo journalctl -u kubelet -f
- Quick disk check: df -h /var | awk 'NR==2{print $4}'

Conclusions so far:
- Most frequent culprit in lab is startup ordering (kubelet started before containerd/socket) and ephemeral disk space. Both have straightforward mitigations.
- The TLS x509 bootstrap errors need correlation with CA rotation events; I suspect some automation rotates CA certs when provisioning many nodes quickly.
- Cgroup mismatches are scary and require an infra-wide policy on kernel/runtime combos.

Next actions (short):
- (high) Implement kubelet systemd drop-in with explicit 'Requires=' for containerd and containerd.socket; add test run.
- (high) Add preflight disk check to provisioning scripts and fail fast if low.
- (med) Create CI matrix job across kernel/runtime versions to surface cgroup regressions.
- (med) Audit code paths that rotate CA or re-issue discovery tokens during scale-ups.
- (low) Replace temporary kubelet cert rotation retry hack with robust verification that apiserver CA is stable at join time.

References / links:
- internal jira: JIRA-PLAT-432 (tracking repro and fixes)
- infra PR with unit change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/912
- sample kubelet log paste: https://paste.redwood.internal/snippet/498a2

Random thoughts / hypotheses to revisit:
- Could SELinux or AppArmor on some images be blocking socket access unexpectedly? Not seen in logs but worth checking.
- Consider using a short-lived systemd timer to delay kubeadm join by 5s if containerd not yet active rather than modifying kubelet unit too aggressively.

End of notes. Will update as I repro more consistently.
